policy: Known production `let _ = <must_use value>` sites a **human wrote**, per file (`clippy::let_underscore_must_use`). Round 85 split the old 152-count: 58 of those findings were not hand-written discards at all but `#[tauri::command]` wrappers, which rustc attributes to the function signature (`expansion: null`, so only the *source line* tells them apart — `scripts/rust-discard-scan.mjs` reads it). Those are reported separately (`macroGenerated` below) and NOT gated: every command adds exactly one, and there is nothing to fix at such a line. What this file gates is the auditable surface. Rounds 85-86 read the rest of it: the daemon (rounds 82-84: `crates/amos-ai`, `amos-supervisor`, `ai_bridge.rs`, `wm.rs`, `amos-android/service.rs`, `assistant_voice.rs`), then the batch this round: **`amos-int`'s output channel** (`try_send` on a *bounded* channel used to drop a `SegmentFinal` silently when the consumer was 128+ behind — now counted and reported, `Session::dropped_outputs()`; a *closed* channel stays silent, that is the documented headless case), **the eight `AppHandle::emit` sites** whose R82-83 label ("Tauri event emission with no listeners") was based on a wrong mechanism — verified in the tauri source: no listener is `Ok` and the JS bridge is only evaluated for windows that registered one, so an `Err` means a *registered* listener could not be reached (the UI never learns) and is now reported per event, **`amos-appstore`'s install-rollback / uninstall bundle cleanup** (the registry is updated either way, so only the log can say that files stayed on disk), **`amos-radio`'s Airplane rollback** (round 85), **`clipboard_guest_link`'s thread join and read timeout** (a panicked ingest thread and an unset timeout both used to be invisible; the timeout is what stops an idle link from hanging `stop()`), **`amos-telephony`'s demo connect** (only the documented `UnknownCall` is ignored now), **`store.rs` / `blocklist.rs` / `sms.rs` mkdir** (the directory failure names itself) and **`amos-int-cli`'s dot-commands** (round 85). Left as explicit, *commented* discards after reading: `Session::fail`'s `set_state` (the guard is the same `allowed` matrix the transition uses, so it cannot fail), `clipboard_guest_link`'s `LINK.set` (single writer inside `get_or_init`), `amos-audio`'s condvar wait (only the elapsed time matters), `amos-clipboard`'s per-connection session, `mail.rs`'s demo seeding, and the gRPC stream frames to a client that disconnected. This file is a RATCHET: a file gaining a hand-written discard, or a new file appearing with one, fails `make lint` until the addition is acknowledged here; a file that drops below its count is reported `[stale]` so the baseline cannot rot. Honest scope: the sites in the files listed above were read one by one, and the ones that hid a real failure were fixed; what is left is deliberate. `macroGenerated` is a snapshot for the reader — the gate prints the live count every run and does not ratchet it (nothing there is actionable). REQ-A187: the scan runs clippy **twice** (plain + every `android` feature), because a clippy-based gate cannot see `#[cfg(feature = "android")]` code at all; measured when added, 113 discard sites existed only in the featured pass and nine of them were real silent failures in the device path (dropped camera frame, unarmed glue bus, undelivered in-call/SMS events, unbound dial/sensor contexts, unwritten self-care report, dropped mic-permission reply) — each fixed by reporting the failure instead of discarding it. What remains above the old 62 is the deliberate `OnceLock::set` exactly-once pattern of the Android attaches, now counted here so the ratchet covers the device surface too. The two passes are de-duplicated by (lint, span) so a feature-independent warning is never counted twice.
